summary.name: Pixel Art
summary.visualIdentity: Explicitly specified 16-bit sprite appearance: low logical resolution, deliberate pixel clusters, whole-pixel placement and discrete colors. A 320×180 canvas and 32-color limit are optional examples, not fixed requirements.
summary.suitableUses: Good for game trailers, looping social clips and clear sprite-based scenes; isometric tile maps suit city-builder explainers. These uses are inferred from the style guidance, not guaranteed outcomes.
summary.limitations: Non-integer scaling, smoothing, antialiased edges and blended post-effects soften pixel clusters and palette boundaries. Keep readable text crisp. Pixel appearance does not prove photographed or game-engine production.
summary.palette: Use task, brand or approved source colors first. Optional six-color suggestion: background #18253A, foreground #F3EBD3, accents #426A76, #8AA386, #D3A45E and #B56D6F. Keep colors discrete; gradients are disabled. Verify contrast in the finished composition.
summary.motionAndInteraction: Animate key poses with few in-betweens, preserving authored exposure rates and holds; place sprites on whole pixels. Palette cycling may change water, neon or day/night colors without shifting silhouettes. Interactive HTML can freeze cycling for reduced motion; use integer scaling and keyboard-accessible tile focus for maps.
summary.audio: No fixed genre, tempo, voice or sound layer is specified. Choose music, narration, effects, ambience or silence for the topic and audience; use inspected audio timing for synchronization, and leave room for speech and reading.
summary.assetRequirements: No mandatory assets are specified. Create indexed sprites or pixel clusters on a fixed-resolution canvas; Aseprite can author sprites and palettes. Preserve supplied artwork and exact colors. Treat the six-color palette as a fallback suggestion only.
summary.combinations: Pixel Art works alone on a fixed grid. Beat-table timing can schedule discrete pose changes and palette cycles; isometric tiles can add spatial depth. Keep cycling discrete, avoid moving every sprite on every beat, and avoid full-screen flashing or arbitrary sprite rotation.
summary.productionApproach: Render with Canvas 2D or a suitable sprite renderer, integer scaling and smoothing disabled; drive visual state from shared seekable time. HyperFrames owns composition, synchronization, validation and export; use Remotion only if HyperFrames is unavailable or a verified required capability is missing. Cache stateful motion for direct and backward seeks.
